name: Single-particle cryo-EM data collection on vitrified 3 mm grids in a Titan Krios at 300 kV with the specimen held near 80 K in vacuum
plain_name: Photograph frozen protein molecules with a 300 kV electron microscope
description: Autoloaded, vitrified 3 mm grids are imaged in a Titan Krios cryo-TEM operated at 300 kV with a direct electron detector; the specimen is kept at about 80 K inside the microscope vacuum to preserve vitreous ice and limit radiation damage.
keywords: Photograph frozen protein molecules with a 300 kV electron microscope

sources.citation: Dickerson JL, Leahy E, Peet MJ, Naydenova K, Russo CJ (2024). Accurate magnification determination for cryoEM using gold. Ultramicroscopy. doi:10.1016/j.ultramic.2023.113883
Zhang Y, Nandy B, Sader K, Russo CJ, Löwe J (2025). Foam film vitrification for cryo-EM. Nature Communications. doi:10.1038/s41467-025-61270-7
Gemin O, Gluc M, Rosa H, et al. (2024). Ribosomes hibernate on mitochondria during cellular stress. Nature Communications. doi:10.1038/s41467-024-52911-4

reported_equipment: FEI Titan Krios G3i electron cryomicroscope

requirements.rationale: The specimen is imaged at about 80 K to keep the ice vitreous.
Electron imaging requires the specimen to be presented in vacuum.
The specimen is a standard 3 mm EM grid (clipped into an AutoGrid for the autoloader).
Vitrified grids are kept in liquid nitrogen until they are loaded into the microscope.
